findings.detail: DISCLOSED_CONTRACT_REVISIONS_P16 says the unhookable value paths 'replace with a callable query, Poly(.., d).eval, string round-trips' are covered by the static AST scan (tests/test_p16.py::_forbidden_calls). The scan detects Poly(...).eval, lambda-query replace and lambdify, but NOT: a named-function callable replace (e.replace(isd, four)), string round-trips (sympify(str(e)).subs(Symbol('d'), 4)), builtin eval(srepr(e)), or a manual expression-tree rebuild -- all four leak a value at runtime (probe). My own broader grep of code/p5_calc + code/p5_entry finds no such use (no eval/exec, no sympify(str(...)), no callable replace), so no released number is affected.

sympify() of a stored string yields a plain Symbol('d') that is NOT the OpaqueDimension: subs/has against dred.d then silently do nothing / return False. Package sites that sympify stored A(d) strings (e.g. batchC premature_d4 mutation sympify(a0).subs(d, 4), d13._opaque_d_refuses, R5_d_retained checks) currently receive sympy objects (the certificates show premature_d4 rejected=True and R5_d_retained=True), but the guard would not protect a future string-based path; e2_evanescent uses locals={'d': d} correctly.

Hardened guard raises for subs, subs(dict), subs(simultaneous), xreplace, replace(d, 4), evalf(subs), N(subs), limit, series in d, Lambda(d, e)(4), Subs.doit, lambdify (default, math, mpmath, sympy), pycode, pickle round-trip + subs. expr.match(d) raises. Not hooked (string outputs, not values): ccode/fcode-type printers; Wild-pattern match (d+1).match(d+w) does not raise despite the docstring 'expr.match(d)' wording (it substitutes no value).
